projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: Consistently high mobile device presence (17-18) paired with zero camera activity over a two-hour window on a Tuesday morning indicates the household is indoors but largely stationary, suggesting a work-from-home or remote learning routine rather than an absence or security event.

Presence signals consistently show 17-18 devices home from 08:41 to 10:24 AM, yet cameras recorded zero activity during this window. This mismatch suggests the camera system may be offline, misconfigured, or in a non-recording mode, creating an unmonitored period while the house is occupied.

The jump to 22 devices at 03:56 AM, combined with zero camera motion and stable presence throughout the early morning hours, confirms routine overnight network behavior rather than physical activity or an intrusion. The home remains secure and undisturbed.

The sudden increase from 21 to 22 connected devices at 03:56 AM, with no camera activity, suggests a device previously out of range (likely in a vehicle or garage) has just reconnected, or a quiet late arrival occurred. This warrants monitoring for a late return or checking garage status to rule out an unreported entry.

The stable presence count (~20 devices) through 00:51 confirms the rest of the household is still home and undisturbed, indicating Steve’s short sleep duration is likely an isolated personal disruption rather than a household event. This matters because it rules out external causes and suggests he is awake alone.
Steve slept only 2.73h last night. May be a rough morning — heads up.

The rapid presence count spike to 21 and drop to 18 within nine minutes (19:43–19:52) occurred with zero camera activity, suggesting either an unmonitored arrival (e.g., via garage or internal door) or temporary Wi-Fi presence detection instability.

The steady increase in connected devices (15 to 19) between 17:21 and 18:49 aligns with typical evening arrivals, but the complete lack of camera observations during this influx suggests the cameras may be offline or misconfigured, leaving the home unmonitored during peak activity.

The combination of a sustained high device count (15–19) with rapid fluctuations and zero camera activity during a weekday afternoon strongly suggests the devices are stationary (likely in a parked car or garage) or a network scanning artifact, rather than active household movement.

The sustained high device count (17–20) with rapid fluctuations during a weekday afternoon strongly suggests the children are hosting friends or streaming, with devices roaming between Wi-Fi zones. This aligns with normal after-school activity, but the fluctuation pattern warrants a quick check to rule out unauthorized network access.
